subject: Fwd: Pilot request - provisional uptime waiver and credits discussion
messages:
From: Sylvia Khan <sylvia.khan@oregrida.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot request - provisional uptime waiver

Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move our internal pilot to the Redwood hosted environment. One ask surfaced from our platform leads: for the first 90 days of the pilot we need a provisional uptime target of 99.0% (rather than the standard 99.95%) for a subset of non-customer-critical batch inference jobs.

Key constraints: 
- The jobs run during nightly maintenance windows and tolerate longer tail latency; failure modes are not customer-facing.
- We need this lower SLO to validate cost/throughput tradeoffs before scaling.
- Oregrida is willing to accept a higher cap on service credits for the pilot period (we proposed a 10% credit cap) and to sign an amendment that reverts to standard SLAs once the pilot completes.

Can Redwood provide a provisional waiver and a short-term SLO amendment? If there are pricing or term tradeoffs (discounts, cap on credits, limits by region), please outline them. Our legal team is on copy (legal@oregrida.com) for a heads up.

Attached: oregrida_pilot_requirements.pdf (1 page)

Best,
Sylvia Khan
VP, Platform Engineering
Oregrida Inc.
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Sylvia Khan <sylvia.khan@oregrida.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot request - provisional uptime waiver and credits discussion

Marissa / Sean — forwarding a pilot request from Oregrida. They want a temporary reduction to 99.0% uptime for a non-customer-facing batch workload for 90 days, and they propose a 10% service credit cap during that period.

Quick thoughts:
- The deviation is material relative to our standard production SLOs; the risk is acceptable for non-customer-facing workloads, but we need to be explicit about regional carveouts and the maximum credit liability.
- Pricing: a small promotional discount or waived setup fee could be a reasonable sweetener.
- Contractually we'll want a hard sunset date and an automatic reversion to standard SLOs with no permanent term change.

Can Deal Desk/RevOps sign off on provisional waiver with conditions below (if needed I can loop in Lauren for exec signoff):
1) Limit pilot to 90 days, single region (us-west-2).
2) Cap total service credit liability to 6% of monthly bill during the pilot (we typically avoid >5%, but can flex for pilot).
3) Require Oregrida to accept a documented SLO amendment and agree to rollback on day 91.
4) Offer a one-time 10% discount on first-month usage as a pilot incentive (trade for the higher credit cap).

Attachments: oregrida_pilot_requirements.pdf (from Sylvia)

Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sylvia Khan <sylvia.khan@oregrida.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot request - provisional uptime waiver and credits discussion

Diego — thanks for the context and the suggested guardrails. I support a conditional approval but want to tighten a couple items before we give an external yes: 

Recommended approach (Deal Desk proposal):
- Approve a 90-day provisional SLO of 99.0% for the named batch jobs, limited to us-west-2 and to the pilot project identifier in the attachment.
- Cap cumulative service credits payable by Redwood to 6% of the monthly invoice for the pilot days (same as your suggestion).
- Exchange: 10% first-month usage credit plus a monthly minimum commit for the pilot of $8,000 (this protects us from extreme credit exposure).
- Require Oregrida to sign proposed-slo-amendment-v1.pdf and accept automatic reversion after 90 days.

I need executive signoff for any exception that increases credit exposure above our standard floor. Lauren — are you comfortable signing off on the 6% cap and the $8k minimum? If you want a smaller cap we can use 5% and increase the first-month credit to 15%.

If approved, we'll route the amendment to legal and set up a DocuSign link (I can coordinate).

Thanks — Marissa
Sr. Manager, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Marissa / team — I reviewed the risk and the commercial trade-offs. Approving the pilot under the proposed Deal Desk terms is acceptable with the following clarifications: 
- Final cap: 6% of monthly invoice during the pilot (no exceptions).
- Minimum monthly committed spend for pilot: $8,000 (non-negotiable).
- Region: us-west-2 only; any cross-region usage voids the waiver.
- Sunset: pilot ends at 90 days; SLOs revert automatically and any extension requires explicit renewed approval.

Marissa — you have exec signoff to proceed and prepare a DocuSign amendment. Diego — please confirm Oregrida accepts the changes (they should be okay with the minimum per your earlier notes).

Lauren Bishop
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
